WindowsCraft 0.14.7 (screens, in-game monitors, gaming monitors and tablets for Cobbleverse)

1. Close Minecraft.
2. Right-click this zip and choose "Extract All...", then open the extracted folder.
3. Double-click "Install WindowsCraft.bat".
   If Windows says "Windows protected your PC": click "More info", then "Run anyway".
4. Start Cobbleverse and join the server as usual.

The server needs this version too: put the same windowscraft .jar into the server's "mods"
folder (delete the old windowscraft .jar there) and restart it. Anyone already on 0.14.2 or
newer is offered this update in chat when they join, and it updates itself (anyone older than
0.14.2 installs it by hand once, like this).

U anywhere: the WindowsCraft menu - all your screens (what's open on them, who can use them,
their size and picture) and the settings.
In-game monitor: look at a black concrete wall or a gaming monitor block and press U (the first
time it offers to install a free display driver). Press O to sit down and use it with your real
mouse and keyboard - it's then shown flat and sharp on your screen like a real monitor, as big
as fits in what you see of the game (never under your taskbar), with the room around it (Alt +
scroll out: still sharp, just smaller); Esc gets up.
Hold Alt and look at your monitor to point and click on it without sitting down.
An app that only runs once (Discord, Calculator...) already open on your desk: opening it from a
monitor brings it over, in the middle of that monitor (and opening it from your own taskbar brings
it back). Each monitor plays only its own sound: a browser opened on a monitor gets a copy of its
own there (sign in once). Full-screen videos stay full screen when you press Esc to get up. U again turns it off; sneak + U opens its menu.
Gaming monitors and tablets: creative tab "WindowsCraft" (or craft them). A gaming monitor faces
you when placed (8 directions). Placed right beside, above or below another one it joins it (no
stand, edge to edge, turned to face you - stand at your seat while placing; sneak to keep it flat)
- joined monitors are joined in Windows too, so windows drag across them.
Each screen's volume (0-500 %): U menu, the slider under its name.
A tablet: holding it turns it on; right-click holds it up (it fills your screen), Esc puts it
down (it keeps playing in your hand), sneak + right-click turns it off.
To share a window or your screen instead: sneak + U on a wall, pick one, Go Live.
On someone else's screen, U opens listening options (3D or direct sound, volume, mute).
Press O while looking at a live screen for theater mode.

If U does nothing or in-game monitors won't turn on: the display driver got stuck. WindowsCraft
now notices that and offers "Repair driver" (Windows asks for permission). Restarting the PC
fixes it too.
If something else about in-game monitors misbehaves: close Minecraft, open the "Windows self-test"
folder and double-click "Run self-test.bat". It takes a couple of minutes (your screens blink and
the mouse moves - leave the PC alone meanwhile) and puts "WindowsCraft self-test" on your desktop:
send that folder's report.
